data.description:
## Problem

`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-g7.eval.yaml` declares `prompt: plan-review-G7` (line 13), and it is the only packaged spec whose filename differs from its `prompt` field (checked over every `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/*.eval.yaml` at origin/main dd72b461814). `load_eval_spec(prompt_id)` (`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:71`) opens `<prompt_id>.eval.yaml` verbatim (`_packaged_eval_spec`, `eval.py:63`), and `calibrate_criterion("G7")` maps the criterion to `criterion_prompt_id("G7") == "plan-review-G7"`.

So on a case-sensitive filesystem (Linux, including the GitHub ubuntu runners):

- `calibrate_criterion("G7")` / `rebar criteria eval G7` raise `EvalError: no eval spec for prompt 'plan-review-G7' at .../plan-review-G7.eval.yaml: [Errno 2] No such file or directory`.
- The `eval-live` loop in `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` takes `pid = spec["prompt"]` (`plan-review-G7`) and calls `run_eval(pid)`, which raises the same uncaught `EvalError` and aborts the step before the specs that sort after it are run.

macOS's default case-insensitive filesystem hides it.

## Evidence

Observed in Gerrit change 3421 patch set 1 CI (GitHub run 44239093717, ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and eval-discipline): `tests/unit/test_eval.py::test_calibrate_criterion_opens_a_gate_session_for_its_solver` called `calibrate_criterion("G7", ...)` and failed with exactly that `EvalError`; the same test passes on macOS. That test was switched to the `necessity` criterion so the change could land; the underlying mismatch is unchanged.

## Expected

The G7 spec loads by its prompt id on every filesystem, and a test asserts that every packaged spec's filename equals its `prompt` field so a future mismatch fails in CI.
data.title: Eval spec plan-review-g7.eval.yaml is named in lower case but its prompt is plan-review-G7, so it cannot be loaded on case-sensitive filesystems
